blocks.body:
## Technical summary

The recommended set is the directly measured Renner A1 combination: `hardness=400 N/mm^p`, `p=2.4`, `epsilon=0.51`, `tau0=0.0004 s`. At the selected `2.0 m/s` reference strike it produces `Fmax=41.8 N`, `1.75 ms` contact duration, normalized peak position `0.185`, rise/fall ratio `0.227`, and impulse `0.0309 N·s`. Across `0.5–6 m/s`, peak force increases monotonically and the impulse remains close to the 15 g hammer's incident momentum.

## A. Current model and approved contact-state correction

The felt law is Stulov's four-parameter hereditary model: `F(t)=F0[u(t)^p−epsilon·h(t)]`, where `tau0·dh/dt+h=u^p`. `p` controls hardening, `hardness` sets the force scale, `epsilon` controls the unloading memory amplitude, and `tau0` controls recovery time. The code now converts the existing metre displacement to millimetres before applying literature values in `N/mm^p`, integrates the exponential history with a piecewise-linear input, and enforces unilateral non-negative contact force.

Because the current explicit one-string waveguide produced non-passive return contacts, one `setVIn()` now admits one complete loading/unloading cycle. A force rise after unloading is treated as a new return-wave contact and is suppressed until the next explicit strike. `StringModel`, force injection, waveguide, delay, dispersion, and loss were not modified.

## B. Literature basis

- [Stulov's hereditary model](https://doi.org/10.1121/1.411912) models felt as a nonlinear material with exponential memory.
- [Stulov's two-model comparison](https://www.ioc.ee/~stulov/ISNA16.pdf) reports `F0=8800`, `p=3.95`, `epsilon=0.992`, `tau0=2 us`, and the equivalent `Q0=70.4`, `alpha=0.25 ms` family; it also reports contact times of `1.6 ms` at `1.31 m/s` and `2.5 ms` at `0.72 m/s` for the fitted experiment.
- [Stulov and Magi's Renner A1 tests](https://www.ioc.ee/~stulov/Device.pdf) report `F0=400`, `p=2.4`, `epsilon=0.51`, `tau0=400 us` from force-compression measurements.
- [Chabassier, Chaigne, and Joly](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.1051/m2an/2013136.pdf) use unilateral positive-part compression, a power-law felt with practical `p` around `1.5–3.5`, and an energy-decaying coupled formulation.
- [Purdue's measured hammer overview](https://www.acs.psu.edu/drussell/Piano/NonlinearHammer.html) documents non-symmetric force pulses and decreasing contact time with increasing force.

## C. Test method and metric definitions

All runs use the project's existing `PianoModel::pianoMovement()` path at `44.1 kHz`, the unchanged `StringModel`, a `15 g` effective hammer mass, and the existing force injection. Only experiment-time parameter configuration and force logging were added to a temporary copy. `hammer_analyzer.py` segments the first event and computes Fmax, the 5%-of-peak contact duration, normalized peak position, rise/fall ratio, impulse, half-maximum width, and force centroid. The analyzer output was also checked against the hammer impulse identity.

## D. Designed parameter combinations

The sweep was deterministic rather than random. It covered published Renner families, one-factor hardness, `p`, `epsilon`, and `tau0` axes, impact-velocity sweeps, and equivalent families that keep `Q0=F0(1−epsilon)` and `alpha=tau0/(1−epsilon)` constant.

### Experiment groups

- **a1_effective_hardness_speed** — Runs: `40`
- **a1_equivalent_speed** — Runs: `45`
- **a1_hardness_speed** — Runs: `35`
- **a1_p_speed** — Runs: `18`
- **epsilon_axis** — Runs: `6`
- **equivalent_family** — Runs: `6`
- **hardness_axis** — Runs: `5`
- **p_axis** — Runs: `6`
- **reference_speed** — Runs: `30`
- **tau_axis** — Runs: `12`

## E. Force-envelope comparison

At `2 m/s`, the corrected single-cycle curves all remain finite. Renner A1 gives a fast loading edge followed by a longer unloading tail. N14 and A3 have similar moderate speed shapes but their microsecond relaxation constants fall below one 44.1 kHz sample, causing strong-contact durations to collapse at higher velocity. The original `p=5`, `tau0=600 us` set is stable through `4 m/s`, but its peak moves extremely early and the `6 m/s` event is too short for the analyzer's five-sample minimum.

### Representative parameter results at 2 m/s

- **Original defaults** — Fmax (N): `53.436`; Duration (ms): `1.542`; Peak position: `0.086`; Impulse (N s): `0.02917`
- **Renner A1 measured** — Fmax (N): `41.804`; Duration (ms): `1.746`; Peak position: `0.185`; Impulse (N s): `0.03087`
- **Renner N14 measured** — Fmax (N): `31.925`; Duration (ms): `1.746`; Peak position: `0.280`; Impulse (N s): `0.03145`
- **Renner A3 soft** — Fmax (N): `30.199`; Duration (ms): `1.111`; Peak position: `0.396`; Impulse (N s): `0.02466`
- **Renner A3 hard** — Fmax (N): `32.169`; Duration (ms): `0.998`; Peak position: `0.417`; Impulse (N s): `0.02384`
- **Hardness 2,200** — Fmax (N): `28.852`; Duration (ms): `1.746`; Peak position: `0.381`; Impulse (N s): `0.03147`
- **Hardness 17,600** — Fmax (N): `33.456`; Duration (ms): `1.769`; Peak position: `0.244`; Impulse (N s): `0.03135`
- **p = 3** — Fmax (N): `30.519`; Duration (ms): `1.769`; Peak position: `0.272`; Impulse (N s): `0.03182`
- **p = 5** — Fmax (N): `33.318`; Duration (ms): `1.746`; Peak position: `0.274`; Impulse (N s): `0.03125`
- **p = 8** — Fmax (N): `36.505`; Duration (ms): `0.522`; Peak position: `0.706`; Impulse (N s): `0.01507`
- **epsilon = 0.98** — Fmax (N): `36.659`; Duration (ms): `1.769`; Peak position: `0.253`; Impulse (N s): `0.03211`
- **epsilon = 0.998** — Fmax (N): `27.660`; Duration (ms): `0.998`; Peak position: `0.490`; Impulse (N s): `0.02113`
- **tau = 0.5 us** — Fmax (N): `36.325`; Duration (ms): `1.769`; Peak position: `0.318`; Impulse (N s): `0.03297`
- **tau = 50 us** — Fmax (N): `37.642`; Duration (ms): `1.156`; Peak position: `0.189`; Impulse (N s): `0.02549`
- **tau = 600 us** — Fmax (N): `50.761`; Duration (ms): `1.587`; Peak position: `0.099`; Impulse (N s): `0.02918`
- **tau = 2,000 us** — Fmax (N): `52.530`; Duration (ms): `1.497`; Peak position: `0.099`; Impulse (N s): `0.02947`
- **N14 equivalent eps .98** — Fmax (N): `31.961`; Duration (ms): `1.746`; Peak position: `0.280`; Impulse (N s): `0.03147`
- **N14 equivalent eps .998** — Fmax (N): `31.912`; Duration (ms): `1.746`; Peak position: `0.280`; Impulse (N s): `0.03144`

## The recommended family remains coherent across velocity

Renner A1 is the only measured family tested here that maintains monotonic Fmax, gently decreasing contact duration, a resolved relaxation process, and `impulse/(m·v)` near one throughout `0.5–6 m/s`. The peak shifts earlier as impact velocity increases, while the unloading tail remains longer than the loading edge.

### Recommended parameters across impact velocity

- **0.5** — Fmax (N): `7.995`; Duration (ms): `1.791`; Peak position: `0.357`; Impulse (N s): `0.00810`
- **0.72** — Fmax (N): `12.460`; Duration (ms): `1.791`; Peak position: `0.301`; Impulse (N s): `0.01154`
- **1** — Fmax (N): `18.488`; Duration (ms): `1.791`; Peak position: `0.256`; Impulse (N s): `0.01582`
- **1.31** — Fmax (N): `25.467`; Duration (ms): `1.791`; Peak position: `0.220`; Impulse (N s): `0.02053`
- **2** — Fmax (N): `41.804`; Duration (ms): `1.746`; Peak position: `0.185`; Impulse (N s): `0.03087`
- **4** — Fmax (N): `92.747`; Duration (ms): `1.655`; Peak position: `0.123`; Impulse (N s): `0.06070`
- **6** — Fmax (N): `146.537`; Duration (ms): `1.610`; Peak position: `0.100`; Impulse (N s): `0.09025`

## Limitations, uncertainty, and robustness checks

The recommendation is conditional on the current one-string, explicit waveguide architecture. Before the approved single-cycle state rule, return contacts created forces up to `8.45e53 N`; parameter tuning alone could not remove that energy gain. The state rule makes the first force envelope usable but deliberately excludes reiterated strikes. It also fixes soft-strike duration near the first return-wave minimum, so the `0.72 m/s` result (`1.79 ms`) does not reproduce Stulov's rigid-target `2.5 ms` result. A true reiterated-contact model would require an energy-consistent coupled update or a choir model, both outside the approved scope.

## Recommended next steps and further questions

Keep this set as the baseline for the current architecture. If reiterated strikes must later be restored, first add an energy audit for hammer kinetic energy plus string energy and obtain approval for an energy-consistent coupled contact update. Do not retune the four felt parameters to compensate for coupling instability.

query.description: Runs the existing PianoModel movement path using the current HammerModel and StringModel, then analyzes the emitted force samples with hammer_analyzer.py.
filters: string model and force injection unchanged
one loading/unloading cycle per setVIn strike

metric_definitions.contact_duration_ms: Time between first and last force samples above 5% of the event maximum.
metric_definitions.peak_position: Peak time normalized to the positive-force contact span.
metric_definitions.impulse_Ns: Trapezoidal integral of contact force over time.
metric_definitions.impulse_over_mv: Impulse divided by hammer incident momentum m*v, with m = 0.015 kg.

query.description: Loads force-time rows emitted by the current HammerModel for the four representative parameter families at 2 m/s.

metric_definitions.time_ms: Elapsed time since the first positive force sample.
metric_definitions.force_N: Non-negative force passed to the existing injection path.
